The Green Cottage, X:8

This is a lovely tune, and I’ve no idea where I got this setting from, or the tune itself. I do love Jackie Daly’s version, where he takes the tune through slowly the first time and then speeds up for the rest of the set. This goes well with “Britches Full of Stitches” in G, and I like to go back to G and chase it with “Maggie in the Woods”, though the Scartaglen (the Sliabh Luachra cousin if you will) would probably go fine with it as well.

↳ Posted by Thady Quill on February 27th, 2016.

The Green Cottage, X:10

I really like this setting in G Dorian on the fiddle. Perhaps not so nice on some other instruments. The G Dorian idea came from one of Anthony Sullivan’s “Session Tunes” books, but this isn’t an exact transcription of that setting. It’s titled there as “The Glen Cottage Polka” and acknowledged from the playing of Jackie Daly.

The Green Cottage, X:12

X:12 is clearly a slightly different setting of the same tune, which is one of several polkas and slides that I picked up from a box player called Nailus O‘Connor in Knocknagoshel, Co. Kerry, in the mid-’80s. I have it (unimaginatively) as ‘O’Connor’s Polka No. 3‘ (a.k.a. ’The Green Cottage’ - though this may not be correct). My outfit plays them in sets as listed in the tune library at www.rudemex.co.uk.

The Green Cottage, X:16 (Denis Doody’s)

Denis Doody’s version of The Green Cottage polka from his 1978 LP that must have inspired Donal Lunny & Co. to record their arrangement of it, which now exists as a separate tune on The Session:

https://thesession.org/tunes/1338

A little nuance that didn’t make it to the ABC is that he added G/F/E instead of GE at the start of the tune when repeating part A.

My guess is that he actually played it in F# minor fingering, since many other sets on that LP feature him playing on a B/C accordion in C#/D style. The second polka in this particular set is in G, but sounds as if it’s played in A major fingering (judging by apparent push & pull patterns etc.)

↳ Posted by Bregolas on January 20th, 2022.

The Green Cottage, X:17 (Julia & Billy Clifford’s)

Julia and Billy Clifford’s version of the tune as played on their Ceol as Sliabh Luachra LP. It is similar to the version now commonly known as Denis Doody’s, but they recorded it in A! Taking this polka to the extreme, with several prominent c’s up there in the second part.

Billy revisited this set with Gerry Harrington on their 2018 CD, Now She’s Purring.

↳ Posted by Bregolas on January 20th, 2022.

Re: The Green/Glen Cottage / … = L’harmonica

Thank you for the 1862 American reference Wes Merchant.
The earlier versions of this tune (or clade of tunes) tend to be the more similar to a French song called L‘harmonica (or Avec l’harmonica); a song with a sailing theme, possibly dating from the turn of the 20th century.
The words to the first verse go;
《Dans mon sac de matelot j‘ai mis tout c’que j’avais de plus beau.. 》

The full lyric (with some -still scant- reference notes) can be perused here;

https://www.wikitrad.org/Page/L%27harmonica
